prerequisites: Completed Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Automotive Engineering or similar.
Basic knowledge of common CAD and CAE tools is required.

learning_outcomes.text: Students have a deepened understanding of the benefits of modeling real requirements such as assembly, manufacturing inaccuracies, and other deviations from nominal dimensions.
Students know further uses of CAE tools such as kinematics simulation, qualitative determination of loads in the design stage.
Students know the preparation of virtual prototypes for real prototyping.
Students know selected innovative methods for real prototyping.
Students have concretely experienced the differences between digital and real prototypes using an application example.

Students have a deepened understanding of abstraction for virtual prototypes and the adapted, manufacturing- and load-appropriate design for selected manufacturing processes suitable for rapid prototype creation.
Students can independently create suitable models for virtual prototypes and purposefully decide on appropriate methods for real prototypes.
Students can critically reflect and explain decision-making situations and related questions regarding the economic efficiency of using virtual or real prototyping methods.
Students can independently carry out existing and future challenges of transferring findings from manufacturing and testing virtual and real prototypes to finished products.

syllabus_topics: Overview of staged digital product model
Consideration of (manufacturing / assembly) tolerances in the digital product model
Kinematic model, inertias, modeling of drive characteristics
Assembly / disassembly in the digital model
Overview of selected manufacturing processes for prototyping
Manufacturing-appropriate design for selected manufacturing processes
Creation of a virtual product model
Derivation of data for manufacturing for different processes
assessment_rules: The term paper involves documenting and presenting the result of a self-developed prototype. The developed product must also be a "real prototype" created using suitable production methods available in the lab.
